TRIAGE DIRECTIVE (operator ruling 2026-10-03): this is an IMPLEMENTATION CHORE. Its specification and design are settled and accepted: openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/ (merged as 7f0aa4ad, council-cleared in run build-decision-0065-slice-two-co-50ef1e34) and decision 0077 (accepted). Do not re-specify or re-design: classify it `chore` so it goes straight to implement. It is still reviewed by the full engine council. If the settled design cannot be implemented as written, the implement seat reports blocked; triage does not reopen the design.

BUILD DECISION 0065, SLICE TWO — UNIT U6c, one narrow visit, ONE pull request. Branch s2/U6c, cut from main at 5b1d6785. Recipe claude-flash-dsh-adv.

READ FIRST: design.md's "Slice two units" preamble and your unit (below, verbatim), the tasks your unit closes in tasks.md, the spec deltas it names, operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md, decision 0077 and decision 0065. Units before yours in your row's Dependencies have landed on main.

THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U6c | U6b | Define and consume the bound plan; 28.1–28.2 | `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/lib.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/broker.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U6c — Define and consume the bound plan

Restart from current main's U6a/U6b; neither held branch is merged. Define the shared closed plan and failure types in protocol/broker.rs, register that public module in protocol/lib.rs, and consume it immediately in CLI broker.rs. Keep native_controls/mcp.rs private for transport checks; this separate protocol edge allows later ledger types to be consumed without another parent visibility edit or duplicate Transport export. The handler validates protected inventory/owner/digest, every plan field and selected box intent, without resolving secrets or spawning. Keep the command's bound-plan and incomplete-serving refusals; no duplicate egress vocabulary or unused public alias. This row deliberately does not create session.rs: its registration/extraction is U6c2.

Closes tasks 28.1 and 28.2; requirements [MB3](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [MB4](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [MB5](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [SC1](specs/slice-two-contracts/spec.md).
Proof: Exact owner/digest/inventory and closed-shape refusals; altered executable/tree/reach/network/bootstrap identity cannot acquire authority. Native OFF and the realm-wide MCP fence stay exact; counters prove zero lookup and spawn.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS VISIT (the-forge-67, 2026-10-06). This is a REPAIR visit. It clarifies the commission.

WHY:
- Run 0065-slice-two-unit-u6c-see-the--584f79f0 built U6c (head c905a1f1). Its council held it: security-hold, high.
- The worktree arrives with that WHOLE attempt applied UNCOMMITTED on current main, so your council judges all of it.
- If quality/file-lines.txt was left out (main moved it), set the rows for the files you touch to their measured `wc -l` counts, in the ledger's `%7d path` format. Touch no other row.
- The chief confirmed: scope is exactly the three allowed production files, every public serving path still refuses, and no redesign is needed. Fix the findings below. Keep everything else.

FINDINGS TO FIX (the chief's numbering):

F1 HIGH: the broker trusts a caller-selected root.
- Today, crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs derives HOME only from the caller's locator (about :148 and :233) and reads the inventory beside it. A self-consistent, owner-only lookalike tree with a true digest reaches ServingIncomplete instead of Unbound. The same caller-derived HOME drives tree's widening check (about :389).
- Fix: D6 says "use the ENGINE-RESOLVED host root". Resolve the trusted host root independently of the locator, through the existing resolver `brokkr_protocol::hands::home_dir` over the broker process's OWN environment. That is the engine's HOME, which the broker inherits.
- Refuse with Unbound any locator whose HOME/.local/state/brokkr/capabilities/ root is not exactly that trusted root. Compare canonical, no-follow identities, not text.
- Use the trusted root, never the locator's, for the widening check.
- Bind each refusal (the lookalike root and the widening check) with an independent removal control.
- Tests must give the broker child the fixture HOME through its environment.
- Drop the "HOME is whatever lies above .local" assumption from evidence/U6c.md.

F2 MEDIUM: Owner identities don't match the engine's.
- protocol/src/broker.rs (about :62) types Owner.effect/attempt/instance as u64, and the CLI demands a decimal attempt directory (about :250).
- The engine's real identities are strings: UUID-string effect and attempt IDs (runtime engine.rs about :1077 and :1377) and a string instance_ref (engine/resume.rs about :373).
- Fix: keep the engine's string representations. Validate the attempt as one safe, nonempty path component.
- Add an engine-shaped ownership control, i.e. a test using UUID-shaped ids.

F3 MEDIUM: positional arrays pass at the typed edge.
- Derived struct Deserialize accepts JSON arrays despite deny_unknown_fields. Inventory, Plan, Owner and `restrictions: []` all reach ServingIncomplete.
- Fix: require object-shaped records at the typed edge, and exactly `{}` for Restrictions.
- Prove-or-refuse, no heuristics. For example, refuse a non-object at each record position before typed decoding, or use a map-only visitor.
- Bind each negative control independently.

F4 MEDIUM: members aren't checked.
- Cardinality and uniqueness are checked (CLI about :304, :326, :333, :352), but these all reach ServingIncomplete: `tools: [""]`, `argv: [""]`, `argv: ["docs-mcp", ""]`, and a server `cap-unrelated` for capability `library-docs`.
- Fix: tool-dialect v1 requires nonempty tool and argv members. D5/0077 requires the server to be exactly `cap-<capability>`.
- Validate these, each with an independent removal control.

F5 MEDIUM: evidence/U6c.md doesn't prove independent removals.
- The recorded removals don't independently prove: source entry/mount bounds, control exclusion, or the StoreInBox predicate. Mutating StoreInBox's display text proves only the text.
- A whole-`well_formed` removal failing only its first assertion proves one check, not each.
- Fix: for each behaviour, record a compiling removal that fails ITS assertion, and the restored pass. Keep it as prose or a compact table. Do not add a fmt/clippy bullet list (that clones slice one's evidence).

F6 LOW: newlines in the invalid-name diagnostic.
- The CLI (about :263) forwards validate_name's plan-controlled invalid name through Refusal::Name. lib.rs's safe_lines keeps newlines, so a name containing LF forges a stderr line.
- Fix inside broker.rs: the diagnostic must not add caller-controlled lines and must keep the required cause. For example, don't echo the name, or render it escaped (one line).
- If it truly can't be fixed in your files, record it and do NOT block.

F7 LOW (run integrity): panel prose contained routing directions. No action. Do not answer it in code.

LATER UNITS OWN THESE. Don't do them here, and don't claim them:
- argv executable resolution and source verification (U6c4, U6c5)
- source/bootstrap reobservation
- network comparison
- identity-based overlap checks

GATES:
- capability_broker tests pass under a root-owned sticky TMPDIR and under an owner-only one. A box /tmp that is group-writable and owned by uid 1000 correctly refuses as Unbound; run with TMPDIR set to an owner-only directory there.
- Run `cargo +1.88 check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`.
- Run quality/ratchet.sh api, files, clones, and baselines origin/main. A public-API rise is expected for the new protocol types; regenerate the snapshot and record it.
- A LOW you can't fix inside your files: record it in evidence/U6c.md and do NOT report blocked.
- Commit everything as ONE signed commit.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U6c.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical

No frozen path (contracts/, fixtures/, reference/, policy/phase-machine.json, extensions/) moved; no unsafe and no new #[allow]. No security hold: the F1 HIGH lookalike-root hole is closed and nothing high/critical remains. Independent confirmation: cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it capability_broker:: -> 20 passed, 0 failed. F1: bound() resolves HOME only via brokkr_protocol::hands::home_dir over this process's own inherited environment, never the locator; HOME must be absolute, is canonicalised, and an unset/relative/non-UTF-8 HOME refuses Unbound. protected_root() opens HOME/.local/state/brokkr/capabilities from / with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, and Layout::open() re-descends the locator one O_NOFOLLOW component at a time, requiring the component in the root position to be that exact directory by (st_dev, st_ino), with euid-/root-owned non-other-writable ancestors (root-owned sticky excepted) and owner-only root-and-below. tree()'s widening check uses the trusted HOME. The only_the_engines_home_roots_a_plan control proves a self-consistent, owner-only lookalike with its true digest and a matching inventory is Unbound, not ServingIncomplete. F2-F6 hold: Owner's effect/attempt/instance are Strings and the attempt is one portable nonempty component equated to its own directory; every one of the 15 records goes through the map-only Object deserializer so positional arrays refuse at each position (Restrictions exactly {}, Tree::System{} struct-shaped); server == cap-<capability> and tool/argv members are nonempty; one_line() escapes control characters so a plan-written binding name cannot forge an LF line (safe_lines also strips control/directional characters per line). Reads are single-handle and fail closed: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat regular, euid-owned, mode 0o077-clear, nlink exactly 1, capped at 1 MiB, digest pinned exactly once in the protected inventory; missing/forged/changed bytes map to Unbound. Every serving path ends in Err(Refusal::ServingIncomplete): no secret value is read, nothing is spawned and nothing is journaled, so the compile fence and native OFF are untouched and no plan can acquire authority in this unit. LOW residual, security-adjacent, for a later visit: crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs:307 one_line() re-implements the canonical refusal-line sink brokkr_protocol::native_controls::bounded_line (native_controls.rs:3524, LINE=512, already imported by the CLI at doctor.rs:17) and drops its 512-scalar bound, so a plan-written binding name can render an unbounded (up to the 1 MiB plan cap) stderr line. This is a 0071-ruling-5 duplicate that also diverges from the one security-control sink; the refusal still fires, control characters are still escaped, and no fail-open or authority is demonstrated, so it is low, not a hold. INFO, no action: the trust anchor is the broker's inherited HOME exactly as D6 and the chief prescribed, so it is only as trusted as the broker's spawner; today that confers no authority because every path refuses, and the serving units must not key authority beyond the broker's own process access on that env-derived root. Also INFO: overlap checks remain lexical, bootstrap digest is shape-only and network/retained/writers.privilege are parsed closed but semantically compared later; the commission assigns these to U6c4/U6c5, reobservation, network comparison and identity-based overlap, and nothing here claims them. This seat is read-only: no fix, no commit.

Tests assert exact (case, refusal) tuples, so per-case removals bind individually; the lookalike control (engine HOME = another dir with its own protected root) only passes the identity check, as claimed. Findings: (1) LOW, ruling 5: CLI broker.rs one_line() (:307) re-implements control-character escaping that brokkr_protocol::native_controls::bounded_line already owns as 'the ONE sink of a capability refusal line' and the CLI already consumes (doctor.rs:17); the copy also drops that sink's 512-scalar bound, so a plan-written name (plan engine-sealed, up to 1 MiB) renders unbounded on one line. (2) INFO: evidence row F1d is labelled 'widening uses the trusted HOME' but its removal deletes the whole widening term; no control distinguishes the trusted HOME from a locator-derived one, which the inode identity check makes indistinguishable anyway, so the label overclaims only in wording. members.security: Security review of U6c (c7031abe against 5b1d6785: cli/src/broker.rs, protocol/src/broker.rs, protocol/src/lib.rs, the capability_broker suite, evidence/U6c.md, tasks.md, quality/). The F1-F6 holds are closed with nothing above low left. F1: bound() takes HOME only from hands::home_dir over the broker's own inherited environment. HOME unset or relative fails closed to Unbound. The trusted root is opened no-follow under the canonical HOME, and the locator's root has to be that same directory by (st_dev, st_ino), not by spelling. Layout::open walks the locator from / with O_NOFOLLOW, judges each component by fstat on the handle it holds, and requires owner-only euid modes from the root down. Each ancestor must belong to euid or root and be writable by no one else unless it is root-owned and sticky. tree()'s widening check now uses the trusted HOME. only_the_engines_home_roots_a_plan binds the lookalike-root control: the same owner-only tree, pinned at its true digest, is Unbound under any other engine HOME. F2: Owner ids are Strings. owns() needs the repo/run/attempt directory components to be equal and the attempt to be one portable component, and a UUID-shaped mismatch control refuses. F3: the Object wrapper sends every record's derived visitor through deserialize_map, so a positional array refuses at each record position, the Inventory, Pin and internally tagged Tree included (13 record controls plus 2 inventory controls). Restrictions accepts exactly {}. F4: members are checked: server == cap-<capability>, and tool and argv members are nonempty, each with its own control. F6: one_line escapes control characters before Refusal::Name and safe_lines sanitizes as well; a control pins that an LF in a name renders as one line. Fail-closed holds: run() still ends in ServingIncomplete after admit, no secret is looked up and nothing is spawned (the FIFO store counter proves zero lookups), no runtime file changed so the MCP compile fence and native OFF are untouched, and the fence test is still present. Nothing is journaled, no secret value is read, and every refusal text is fixed except decision 0012's name cause, which is escaped. Plan and inventory reads are owner-only, single-link and regular files, opened no-follow and capped at 1 MiB. LOW residual, for U6c2-U6f: the trust anchor is the broker's inherited HOME (as D6 and the chief ruled), so any process that can exec brokkr with its own HOME can root its own owner-only tree. Today that confers nothing, because every path refuses with ServingIncomplete. The serving units must not let an admitted plan reach a secret store or privilege beyond the invoking process's own reach, or they must anchor the store the same way. As commissioned, overlap, reach and store-exclusion checks are still textual and executable resolution is not done yet; U6c4/U6c5 and the identity-overlap units own those, and nothing here wrongly claims them. Not run by this seat: cargo test was refused by this seat's sandbox (cargo is not granted). The verify phase recorded a pass.
members.spec-compliance:
Reviewed the entire 5b1d6785..c7031abe diff against U6c/tasks 28.1-28.2, MB3/MB4/MB5/SC1, D5/D6, the operator ruling, decisions 0065/0077 and decision 0071. Production scope is exactly the three authorized files; frozen paths are unchanged. No settled specification or design defect was found.

LOW SC-1 — The shared records expose a second, permissive public decoding entry point (crates/brokkr-protocol/src/broker.rs:40-45, 70-72, 90-92 and the other remote derives). Deriving Deserialize with remote = Self on a public record generates a public inherent Type::deserialize. Only the trait implementation wraps that decoder in Object. An external scratch Rust probe against the built library confirmed Restrictions::deserialize on [] returns Ok, Owner::deserialize accepts its six-element positional array, Inventory::deserialize accepts [[]], and Tree::deserialize accepts ["package","/opt/docs"]. serde_json::from_str::<Restrictions>("[]") correctly refuses. Thus the current CLI edge is protected, but the shared public decoding API contradicts F3's object-only record contract and exposes a helper that only needs internal visibility (0071 rulings 3 and 6). Keep the raw derived decoder private or ensure every exposed decoder enforces the object shape; bind that API behavior with exact tests and removal evidence.

LOW SC-2 — Task 28.2's per-new-test mutation evidence is incomplete (openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U6c.md:165-234; crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker.rs:277). The evidence mentions R3 at line 166, but its table ends at R2 and contains no text-pin mutation. Record that test's actual mutation/restoration result to substantiate the completed checkbox (0071 ruling 9). This is implementation evidence debt, not a defect in the accepted task breakdown.
